- Confirmation would come from a MACD histogram that keeps widening and RSI staying under 30.
- Any bounce that fails near the 10 EMA (about 69.75k) or the 200 SMA/VWMA cluster (about 72–73k) fits a bear-market rally pattern.

  - Consecutive closes above 65,363, then above 69.75k.
  - The MACD histogram stops getting more negative.
  - RSI climbs back above 30 and holds.
  - Volume stays above average on up days.

The only sentiment we have has retail posting "up only," "bulls relentless," "buying continues" and "just go to $1,000,000." That is a market that hasn't been washed out. One wants to "sweep $61K," and another expects retracements into the $60s. One poster calls the day's action a "pump and dump." Your thesis needs fear to be exhausted, and the available evidence shows hope still intact.

## 6. Macro isn't "priced in," it's absent

A 98% chance of no Fed cuts in 2026 means there's no easing tailwind to ignite a recovery. "Nothing left to disappoint" is not a reason to buy. You need a catalyst, and none appears in the data. Cross-asset signals point the wrong way. Gold and silver are at one-year lows, so BTC isn't benefiting from any alternative-store-of-value bid, and chip stocks fell on new US restrictions, which hits the high-beta tech risk appetite BTC has traded with. These are headlines only and the causes weren't given, so I treat them as caution flags, not proof. But they make a "pure upside optionality" argument hard to sustain.

## 7. No valuation floor

The fundamentals tool returned no balance sheet, cash flow or income data, which is expected for BTC. There is no earnings yield or book value to say "this is cheap." Price is set by flows and sentiment, the very things we lack data on. The "golden cross" configuration in the fundamentals report is a lagging artifact of averages that were built during the rally and are rolling over now. It tells us about where price was, not where it's going.

## What I concede, and what would change my mind

- I don't have ETF flows, on-chain data, funding or BTC-specific news either. My case rests on price structure, prediction markets and thin sentiment, so it's a trend call, not a certainty.
- A relief rally toward 69.75k is plausible. I'd treat it as an opportunity to reduce exposure, not to add.
- A close above 65,363 alone changes little. Closes above 69.75k, a MACD histogram that stops widening, and a reclaim of the 72–73k cluster would force me to rethink. Absent those, rallies are for selling.

## Bottom line

You've built a careful tactical long, but nearly every pillar leans on a signal that hasn't confirmed: RSI oversold without divergence on closes, volume that was exceeded 11 days earlier, a bounce that failed to follow through, a mean-reversion target that keeps falling, and a stop that is both close to noise and not truly defined. Meanwhile the market-implied tail favors a further leg to $55k or $50k, and the upside is capped by an overhead supply cluster you admit exists. The prudent stance is to stay underweight or avoid new longs, and to treat any bounce into 69.75k to 73k as a place to sell, with 62,018 as the line that opens 59k and then 57.7k.
